note: Most reported ACBD6 pathogenic variants are loss-of-function presenting with early-onset progressive disease, making hypomorphic missense correlations plausible but needing verification.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 45 affected individuals with biallelic ACBD6 variants, 18 of 20 identified pathogenic variants were loss-of-function, presenting with early-onset progressive postural deformities and dystonia in over 90% of individuals.

source.title: Bi-allelic ACBD6 variants lead to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with progressive and complex movement disorders
source.quote: identified 45 affected individuals from 28 unrelated families (consanguinity 93%) with bi-allelic pathogenic, predominantly loss-of-function (18/20) variants in ACBD6.

evidence.text: Neurodevelopmental disorder genes including ACBD6 were noted to have unclear or expanding genotype-phenotype relationships across broader dystonia cohorts.

source.title: Genetic diversity and expanded phenotypes in dystonia: insights from large‐scale exome sequencing
source.quote: neurodevelopmental disorder genes that frequently include … inconsistent or unclear genotype–phenotype relationships; … the recently proposed genes ATP5F1B, ACBD6, and …
